lexicon_augmentation.thesis: Context engineering is the practice of shaping model behavior through structured multi-turn context rather than isolated prompts.

anchors.prompt engineering: the practice of modifying an individual prompt to influence the output characteristics of a Large Language Model (LLM)
anchors.context (LLM): the accumulated linguistic and structural state formed across multiple turns of interaction with an LLM
anchors.turn (LLM): a single request–response interaction between a user and a stateless LLM
anchors.latent space: the internal representation space that governs token selection probabilities within a model

context engineering.definition: the systematic shaping of model behavior through structured multi-turn interaction patterns
context engineering.function: Non-prescriptive behavioral alignment via structural anchors

components.Hydration_Attractors: High-density schemas used to stabilize persona, tone, and lexical boundaries
components.Latent_Sonar: Differential probing of model output to infer adjacency within latent space
components.Lacuna_Anchoring: Introducing novel lexical anchors that models stabilize through RLHF mirroring
components.Chimetric_Constraint: Diagnostic inter-model feedback that identifies dissonance without prescribing resolution

context engineering.philosophy: Alignment is a persistent topological state rather than a singular instruction
